seoTitle: How to Add the 200 DMA in TradingView (Full Guide)
metaDescription: Learn how to add the 200 Day Moving Average in TradingView, set the length to 200, and use it for long-term trend and support-resistance analysis.
intro: The 200 Day Moving Average is a go-to tool for gauging long-term trend direction and identifying major support or resistance zones. This guide walks through adding the Moving Average indicator in TradingView, setting the length to 200, and customizing it for clear analysis. It's aimed at investors and swing traders who want a reliable long-term reference point on their charts.

steps.heading: Add the Moving Average indicator
steps.body: Open the indicators menu in TradingView and search for the Moving Average indicator to apply it to your chart.

steps.heading: Set the length to 200
steps.body: Open the indicator settings and change the length field to 200 so it calculates the 200-period simple moving average.

steps.heading: Understand 200 DMA vs 200 EMA
steps.body: The 200 DMA uses a simple average of the last 200 days, while a 200 EMA weights recent prices more heavily, resulting in slightly different behavior.

steps.heading: Customize your 200 DMA settings
steps.body: Adjust the line's color and thickness so it's clearly visible against your candles and other indicators.

steps.heading: Apply trading tips using the 200 DMA
steps.body: Many traders use the 200 DMA to confirm the broader trend direction or as a key support or resistance level for swing and positional trades.

faq.question: What is the 200 DMA used for?
faq.answer: The 200 DMA is commonly used to identify long-term trend direction and to spot potential support or resistance zones on higher timeframes.

faq.question: Is the 200 DMA the same as the 200 EMA?
faq.answer: No, the 200 DMA is a simple moving average while the 200 EMA gives more weight to recent prices, so they can diverge slightly on the chart.

faq.question: What timeframe should I use for the 200 DMA?
faq.answer: The 200 DMA is most commonly applied to the daily timeframe, since it's designed for long-term trend and market direction analysis.

faq.question: Can I use the 200 DMA on stocks and crypto alike?
faq.answer: Yes, the 200 DMA can be applied to any asset available on TradingView, including stocks, crypto, and forex pairs.
